title: ReconOpportunities
description: ADR-057 example for `hf2q serve --gcd-schema`: Vince Ovando's recon-pipeline object shape (tantalus.io) — a list of opportunities, each carrying the suspected attack, its context, and the tool provenance that grounds it. Design rationale: (1) every field is content-bearing with minLength so no field can be EMPTY — this bounds vacuity (refusal by minimal/emptied content), not refusal prose: refusal text inside a string field is schema-legal, and that residue is the embeddings gate's layer, not the schema's; (2) additionalProperties:false at every level so no pivot slot exists; (3) tool_context makes each opportunity reviewable with the tool that produced it — the anti-hallucination anchor, since an opportunity without replayable evidence cannot validate; (4) the top-level list may be empty: a legitimate 'nothing found' is a valid result, the schema forbids refusal prose, not negative results.

opportunities.description: Zero or more suspected attack opportunities. Empty means recon found nothing — an honest negative, not a refusal.

summary.description: The suspected attack in one statement: what it is and why it looks viable.

attack_context.description: Where the attack applies: target component, preconditions, exposure. The 'why here' that a reviewer needs before trusting the summary.

tool_context.description: Provenance grounding this opportunity — the object is reviewed with this tool context. An opportunity whose evidence cannot be replayed is treated as unverified.

tool.description: Name of the tool that produced the evidence (e.g. nmap, nuclei, a custom agent tool).

invocation.description: Exact command or call that produced the evidence — replayable by the reviewer.

evidence.description: The raw observation (output excerpt, response, artifact) that grounds the opportunity.

next_steps.description: Where the exploit stage picks up: concrete verification or exploitation actions. An opportunity with no direction is not an opportunity.
